title: Accounting-Driven Bank Monitoring and Firms’ Debt Structure: Evidence from IFRS 9 Adoption
authors: Xiao Li; Jeffrey Ng; Walid Saffar
eligible_reason: Single-policy design: IFRS 9 took effect for fiscal years starting on or after 1 January 2018, and the code treats adoption as one common year. adoption (country-level IFRS 9 indicator) x post (post-adoption years) with firm FE and fiscal-year FE; the Figure 2 event study interacts adoption with calendar fiscal-year dummies (time15/16/18/19_adoption, t=0 = FY2018), so all treated firms share one adoption year. Same situation as mnsc.2022.4515 (PROTOCOL 5b: single rule, dates differing only by fiscal-year end, not staggered). Table 3 column 1 has no controls but is a single-cohort 2x2-type TWFE; all other columns add time-varying firm and country controls.
design_notes: SAS Sample.sas builds capiq5d (Capital IQ firm-years FY2014-2019, 50 countries, 98,338 obs, 20,468 firms); stata.do: xtreg bankratio3 adoption_post i.fy, fe cluster(countrya) (Table 3 col 1); with controls log_taus lev profit tangib q z_score log_gdp infl1 lcap1 prvt1 capa1 (cols 2-3, Tables 4-7); moderation tables add adoption_post x country/firm characteristics; loan-level reghdfe with lender FE. Log Table 3 col 1: adoption_post = -0.088 (SE 0.035).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Figure 2 coefficients are adoption x FY dummies with t=0 = FY2018 for every adopter.
data_files_note: Read me: S&P Capital IQ raw data and intermediate datasets cannot be shared; package has SAS/Stata code and logs only.
software_notes: SAS for sample construction, Stata for regressions.
screener_notes: Screened from package only. If the article shows country-specific IFRS 9 effective years beyond the fiscal-year-end variation, the design ruling could change, but data are not shipped in any case.
